analysis:
The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md: the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and a new 'Add-On Hold' test-documentation section (head lines ~767-790 per the changed range map). The supplied head_text excerpt ends at line 474, so the new section is visible only in the truncated patch excerpt, which cuts off mid-sentence ('The peer check is exercised only neg...'). The base unit is the old file's tail context, with no modified lines visible. No code, config, workflow or security control changes are in this batch.

The documented commands run local test suites (AddonIPCTests, AddonHoldStoreTests, AddonPeerPolicyTests, AddonIPCServerTests and others) that bind a real AF_UNIX socket and take a flock in a private temp runtime directory. No model weights, credentials or live provider state are needed. The docs state that the real peer policy refuses the test process, that unauthenticated peers and stale or live sockets are tested, and that update and reconnect cannot reopen a hold. These are test-coverage claims, not implementation.

The underlying add-on hold feature (a local IPC hold that unloads models and drains, with the hold carried in register and heartbeat messages) is not in the supplied evidence. It touches TB-002 (coordinator-to-provider websocket: draining heartbeat, registration encoding) and TB-003 (local operator versus process: peer policy, socket permissions). It also touches the availability threats T-010 and T-029 and the TB-011 authorization lifecycle.

The canonical threat model has no entry for the add-on hold IPC surface, so the source PR that implements it should be reviewed for peer authentication, socket permissions, hold lease expiry, and any new coordinator-visible fields. The new section is not documented as invalidating any threat assumption, and the T-041 cache content is unaffected. No finding is raised from docs alone.
